acceptedHighFindings.rationale: Debian trixie remains vulnerable in an SQLite FTS5 MATCH path that requires a crafted SQLite database. Academy production uses PostgreSQL and neither ingests attacker-provided SQLite databases nor executes application FTS5 queries.

Debian trixie remains vulnerable in an SQLite FTS5 MATCH path that requires a crafted SQLite database. Academy production uses PostgreSQL and neither ingests attacker-provided SQLite databases nor executes application FTS5 queries.

The affected glibc ungetwc path requires an exotic overlapping character encoding and does not affect standard Unicode encodings. Academy Python entrypoints use standard Unicode and do not expose native wide-character pushback to product input.

The affected GLib path requires malformed GVariant deserialization. Academy OCR entrypoints do not accept or deserialize untrusted GVariant values, and product payloads are handled by Django and Python serializers.
The affected GLib path requires constructing an invalid GDateTime value. Academy OCR entrypoints do not expose GLib date construction to product input and application dates are validated in Python.
The affected GLib regular-expression path requires G_REGEX_RAW case escaping. Academy OCR entrypoints do not compile product input through GLib regular expressions or use the G_REGEX_RAW mode.
The affected GLib path requires a multibyte GIOChannel line terminator. Academy OCR entrypoints do not expose GIOChannel parsing to product input and use Python file streams instead.
The affected GLib path requires a crafted locale key file with an empty value. Academy OCR entrypoints do not load user-provided GLib key files or expose locale key parsing to product input.
The affected GLib path requires interaction with a malicious D-Bus server. Academy OCR containers do not use D-Bus for product work and do not accept D-Bus server endpoints from users.

Debian trixie has no stable fix for this client-side publickey response overflow. Academy runtime containers are ARM64 and expose no SSH, SFTP, SCP, Paramiko, or libssh2 client path; libssh2 is present only through the Tesseract and libcurl package chain.

Debian trixie has no stable fix for this malicious SSH publickey-subsystem response path. Academy runtime entrypoints never create SSH or libssh2 client sessions; the package is a non-invoked transitive dependency of the OCR runtime.

Debian trixie remains vulnerable in the SFTP open response path. Academy API, AI, and Tools entrypoints do not open SSH or SFTP sessions, and production remote administration is owned by host-side AWS SSM rather than container libssh2.

Debian trixie has no stable fix for this malicious SSH server handshake path. Academy runtime code has no outbound SSH client entrypoint, so it cannot negotiate the affected AES-GCM session through the transitive libssh2 package.

Debian trixie remains vulnerable in the SSH publickey listing parser. Academy runtime processes neither connect to SSH servers nor invoke the libssh2 publickey subsystem; the library is retained only by the stable OCR dependency chain.

Debian trixie has no stable fix for this malicious SSH server packet path. Academy runtime images are ARM64 and contain no outbound SSH client flow, while operational commands use AWS SSM outside the application containers.

The affected xdgmime parser requires an attacker-controlled MIME magic database in a user-writable XDG data directory and a GLib content-type guess call. Academy API, AI, and Tools containers expose no local user session, never load product files as an XDG MIME database, and use Python validators rather than GLib MIME detection. Debian trixie has no stable fix, so this exact identity is accepted only until the stated expiry.

The PCRE2 issue requires an attacker-controlled recursive DFA regular expression together with the native pcre2_dfa_match workspace path. Academy runtime entrypoints do not call PCRE2 or expose native regular-expression compilation; product matching uses Python's re engine. Debian trixie has no fixed package yet and classifies this as no-dsa/minor, so only this exact identity is accepted until expiry.

The zlib issue requires non-blocking native gzwrite followed by gzprintf or gzvprintf after a write stall. Academy uses Python zip and bounded zlib decompression paths and does not call the native formatted gzip-write APIs. Debian trixie and unstable have no fixed package yet, so only this exact identity is accepted until expiry.

The libxml2 issue is in xmlSnprintfElements while formatting DTD validation content models. Academy upload extraction uses Python ElementTree, HWPX output creates an application-owned tree without DTD validation, and the Video FFmpeg build enables only libx264 after disabling external-library autodetection, with no libxml2 call path. Debian trixie has no fixed package, so only the four observed runtime identities are accepted until expiry.
